signals.text: Behaviour, rewards and sanctions We promote good behaviour through a simple and consistent system of positives and negatives, set out in the Behaviour, Character and Discipline Policy and displayed on the positives and negatives poster around the school.

Positives are earned for good work, hifz, kindness, khidmah (service), a tidy room and much more, and are spent on rewards; negatives are recorded in the behaviour log with the reason, are always explained to the pupil at the time, and lead to weekend detention with a reflection activity.
Darul Uloom London reserves the right to suspend, exclude or expel any student who breaches the rules of the institute, following the procedure in the Behaviour, Character and Discipline Policy (03).

It is a very serious offence to bring cigarettes, shisha pens, vapes, drugs or any such items into the school, and it leads to permanent exclusion under the Behaviour, Character and Discipline Policy.

Welcome to Darul Uloom London School
An independent boarding school for boys aged 11 to 19 in Chislehurst, offering a full secondary education and sixth form within an Islamic environment.
About Us
Darul Uloom London was established in 1988 and is situated in Chislehurst, London. The surroundings are very attractive and peaceful and the school is easily accessible from all directions.
Daily congregational prayer, Islamic manners and dress, and Islamic sessions alongside the secular curriculum.
Darul Uloom London prides itself on its delivery of a high standard of education.
Our supportive boarding environment allows pupils to develop.
Our good balance of academic study prepares pupils for life beyond Darul Uloom London.
Our pupils grow up within an Islamic environment that shapes their character, manners and sense of service, preparing them to contribute positively to the Muslim community and to wider British society.
Teaching & Learning
Secular Curriculum
We teach a broad secular curriculum to GCSE and, in the sixth form, to A level and vocational diplomas.
Islamic Environment
Daily life at the school is built around the five daily prayers, Islamic manners and dress, and Islamic sessions including Hifz (memorisation of the Holy Qur’an) and Alimiyyah studies (Islamic theology and scholarship).
What parents say
We chose Darul Uloom London because we wanted our child to grow in an Islamic environment – one where faith is part of everyday life, good character is nurtured, and a love for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is at the heart of everything they do.
Parent of a Year 7 pupil
Over the past three years at Darul Uloom London, we have seen our child grow in faith, confidence and character. Being surrounded by an Islamic environment has helped strengthen their connection with Allah and made practising their faith a natural part of everyday life.
Parent of a Year 10 pupil

About Us
About the school · Welcome from the Principal · Our aims and Islamic environment · Additional needs · Premises · Governance · Support the school
Welcome from the Principal
Welcome to Darul Uloom London School. We pride ourselves in delivering the highest standard of education within an Islamic environment. We ensure the learning process and growth of each child is well-rounded, academically, morally, spiritually, athletically and creatively.
This website is intended to give you an insight into some of the important workings of the school and to reflect our ethos and expectations. It cannot replace the day-to-day vibrancy of life at the school and its boarding environment. We strongly recommend finding some time to come and see us in action. We aim to provide a welcoming environment for all our guests and visitors.
With the correct inspiration and challenge, we believe that every child can succeed in life
We aim to support this through a strong academic curriculum, delivered within an Islamic environment and supported by our outstanding and ever-improving extra-curricular provision. Our blend of traditional values combined with innovation and creativity provides a rich environment for development and growth.
We aim to create an environment of opportunities for all our pupils. In exchange, students are expected to work hard and in an exemplary fashion. Darul Uloom London School makes a significant difference in the lives of our young people and we very much look forward to welcoming your son and helping them achieve their full potential.
May Allah assist us and accept our endeavours. Ameen. Wa ‘alaykum al-salaam
Maulana Ubaid, Principal
Our aims and Islamic environment
In common with all Muslims, our aim is to live our lives in accordance with the wishes of Allah.
Our hope is that, by providing a high-quality secular education within an Islamic environment, in accordance with the Noble Qur’an and Sunnah of our Beloved Prophet (saw), our pupils will grow into young men who practise Islam with understanding and serve the Deen of Allah. Our Islamic sessions support pupils who wish to memorise the Qur’an (Hifz) or pursue Alimiyyah studies, and our hope is that some will go on to become imams and religious leaders, serving the Muslim community in the UK and making a positive contribution towards social cohesion in our multicultural society.
The school helps children to explore and develop their Islamic identity as a natural part of their mental, emotional and personal development. The school aims to prepare Muslim pupils to be good Muslims and responsible citizens; to embed in each pupil a sense of discipline; and to enable them to grow up to become upright, respectable and worthy citizens of their respective countries.
The values of the school go hand in hand with the promotion of the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
The Islamic environment of the school is of the utmost importance. To sustain it, Darul Uloom London places a strong emphasis on the five daily prayers in congregation, Islamic manners and behaviour, punctuality, Islamic dress, mutual respect between pupils, and the utmost respect for staff and parents.
Ethos Statements
Children and young people are part of our community, entrusted upon us by Allah. It is therefore our duty, our responsibility and our privilege to nurture them in learning moral values and in obedience to Allah.
We aim to educate our children to participate effectively and constructively within society from within a spiritual, Quranic, and Prophetic perspective through the means of example, dialogue, and positive communication.
Support for pupils with additional needs
Special educational needs and disabilities. Our SENCO is Tazmul Islam, our Head of Education, who can be contacted through the school office. We welcome applications from pupils with special educational needs or disabilities and make reasonable adjustments in line with our Equality, Accessibility and Religious, Dietary, Language and Cultural Needs Policy and our Accessibility Plan. Where a pupil has an Education, Health and Care (EHC) plan, we work with the pupil’s home local authority and his parents to provide the support set out in the plan and to review it annually.
English as an additional language. Pupils who have difficulty in English are supported by the school working together with the English teachers to provide additional support in the following ways:
Premises
The school is a purpose-built hostel constructed in 1974. Its premises comprise 130 modern boarding rooms in addition to classrooms, a dining hall, an assembly hall, a prayer hall, playing fields and two car parks with over 70 spaces. The site extends to 10 acres. All 130 rooms have standard facilities including cupboards and drawers, full carpeting, beds and mattresses. Each room is generally shared by two or three boys.
An extension was built in 2007 consisting of 18 classrooms, a science laboratory, a prayer hall and wudhu facilities.
Governance and management
Darul Uloom London School is an independent boarding school for boys. The proprietor is Darul-Uloom London, a registered charity (charity number 1043305) governed by a Board of Trustees. The proprietor’s principal office is at Darul Uloom London, Foxbury Avenue, Chislehurst, BR7 6SD (telephone 020 8295 0637).

Safeguarding at Darul Uloom London
Safeguarding is central to everything we do. Darul Uloom London is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, in accordance with section 157 of the Education Act 2002 and Keeping Children Safe in Education, and expects all staff, volunteers, trustees and visitors to share this commitment.
Safeguarding children is defined in Working together to safeguard children as:
protecting children from maltreatment
preventing impairment of children’s health or development
Our safeguarding team
A trained deputy is always contactable during school and boarding hours, including overnight. All members of the safeguarding team hold Level 3 child protection training and are trained for the DSL role.
Principal and Prevent lead: Maulana Ubaid
Safeguarding Trustee: Muthiur Rahman
Chair of Trustees: Mohammed David Khan
If you are worried about a child
Our safeguarding policies
Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy (PDF) – reviewed 28 August 2026, in force from 1 September 2026
To access all other policies, please follow this link.
Boarders
Every boarder can talk to any adult he trusts, to the Head of Boarding and Designated Safeguarding Lead, or to one of two independent listeners who are not school staff and can be telephoned directly at any reasonable time. Their details are in the Boarders’ Booklet and on the boarding noticeboards, with the free helplines above. Boarders and parents may also raise a concern about a boarder’s welfare with Ofsted, which inspects boarding welfare: 0300 123 1231 or enquiries@ofsted.gov.uk.
Prevent and British values
The school has a legal duty to have due regard to the need to prevent people from being drawn into terrorism. The Principal is the school’s Prevent lead; concerns are reported to the Designated Safeguarding Lead and handled under the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy. The school actively promotes the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
Online safety
The school’s internet is filtered and monitored to keep pupils safe, and every pupil signs an acceptable use agreement. Our e-Safety Policy explains the arrangements. We keep parents up to date with new and emerging online risks through parents’ evenings, newsletters and this website.
CEOP (the Child Exploitation and Online Protection Command) is part of the UK’s National Crime Agency and works nationally and internationally to bring online child sex offenders to justice.

Parents
Contacting the school · The school day · Term dates and leave · Uniform and personal appearance · Smoking and illegal items · Fees · What parents say
At Darul Uloom London, we are committed to working with parents to secure the best educational outcomes and to understand the individual needs of every child. This means that children, parents and teachers are able to have their say, be heard appropriately, and have clear and efficient communication that is respectful to all parties.
Contacting the school
If you would like to contact a member of staff, we would ask that you call reception or email education@darululoomlondon.com
Our support staff will pass this message onto the relevant member of staff. We ask that you phone to request appointments to meet with staff and do not turn up without one, in order to avoid disappointment.
During the school day, we want teachers to prioritise teaching and learning and pastoral care. They may not, therefore, be available to respond to messages or emails immediately.
Our aim is to respond to your phone call or email within 48 hours. If the query is complex then a holding phone call or email will be used within 48 hours, so that we are able to provide a full response.
In an emergency or out of office hours, please use the emergency contact numbers given to you in the Boarders’ Booklet at the beginning of each academic year. A copy of the Boarders’ Booklet is on the Policies & Documents page, or can be requested from the school office.
Have you changed your address or contact numbers, or has your son’s medical information changed? If so, please tell the school at once by email to education@darululoomlondon.com, so that we can keep him safe and keep in touch with you.
The school day
Here is a brief overview of the school day. Salah is prayed at its appointed time every day and the timetable is built around it; prayer times change through the year.
Fajr salah (dawn prayer)
Breakfast in the dining hall
Preparation for the Islamic session, including wudu (ablution)
Islamic session continues
Zuhr salah (midday prayer)
Mutala is in the Masjid
Isha salah (night prayer)
Term dates and leave
The holiday and term dates, examination dates and training days are published here and in the holiday planner before the start of each year, and are given to parents at the beginning of the year. Year 7 pupils go home every weekend; from Year 8, pupils go home every other weekend. When returning from a weekend or holiday, pupils must be back in school and signed in before the gates close at 5.30pm.
There is no entitlement to leave in term time, and the school does not authorise family holidays or travel in term time; please plan family travel within the school holidays. Short leave for a hospital appointment, or for a wedding or funeral in the immediate family, must be requested by email to education@darululoomlondon.com at least 72 hours before the leave; an emergency such as a bereavement is dealt with at once by telephone. Additional leave of more than one day is requested on the leave form, with evidence, at least four weeks in advance where the event is foreseeable, and is granted only by the Principal in exceptional circumstances. Absence taken without permission is recorded as unauthorised and may be referred to Bromley’s Education Welfare Service, which can issue a penalty notice (£80 per parent if paid within 21 days, rising to £160), and may put your son’s place at risk. Full details are in the Attendance Policy including Additional Leave on the Policies & Documents page.
Uniform and personal appearance
Pupils must at all times wear clothes conforming to Islamic law (Sharia) and adhere to the practices of our Holy Prophet (PBUH) with regard to personal appearance. This means that you must wear a topi (cap) and a white jubbah or shalwar kameez. The only jumper pupils are permitted to wear is a plain black jumper with no logo; hoodies are not allowed. Hair must be cut to one level, in accordance with the Sunnah, and the beard must not be trimmed, plucked or shaved.
Smoking and illegal items
Smoking and vaping are strictly prohibited. It is a very serious offence to bring cigarettes, shisha pens, vapes, drugs or any such items into the school, and it leads to permanent exclusion under the Behaviour, Character and Discipline Policy. If you are not sure whether something is allowed, it is the responsibility of the pupil and his parent or guardian to check before bringing it on site.
Mobile phones and devices
Darul Uloom London is a mobile-phone-free school. Mobile phones, tablets, smartwatches and games consoles are not allowed at school, including in boarding. A phone that is found will be confiscated and donated to charity or, at the school’s discretion, returned to parents at the end of the year. The only exception is a device needed for a medical condition (for example a glucose monitor), agreed in writing with the Head of Boarding before it is brought in.
Fees
Information about fees is under review and will be published here shortly. In the meantime, please contact the school office on 020 8295 0637 or education@darululoomlondon.com for the current fee schedule and payment options.
What parents say
Parents tell us that, above all, they choose Darul Uloom London for its Islamic environment. Here is what some of them say.
“We chose Darul Uloom London because we wanted our child to grow in an Islamic environment – one where faith is part of everyday life, good character is nurtured, and a love for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is at the heart of everything they do.”Parent of a Year 7 pupil
“Over the past three years at Darul Uloom London, we have seen our child grow in faith, confidence and character. Being surrounded by an Islamic environment has helped strengthen their connection with Allah and made practising their faith a natural part of everyday life.”Parent of a Year 10 pupil
Quotations are published with the parent’s written consent and are reviewed each year.

Admission
How we admit pupils · Step by step · Criteria · How to apply · Terms and conditions · Declaration · Your information
How we admit pupils
Darul Uloom London admits boys aged eleven and above (of secondary school age). The main entry point is Year 7, where we admit around 30 pupils each year; we also admit a small number of pupils into Years 8, 9 and 10 and into the sixth form when places are available. Admission is by entrance tests in English and mathematics, an interview, and a report and reference from the pupil’s current school. Interviews are usually conducted by the Head of Administration and/or the Head of Boarding and Designated Safeguarding Lead, and are conducted objectively without questions that imply racial or religious bias.
The application form and all required documents must be completed before a pupil can be admitted; until the application is complete, a pupil will not be officially admitted.
As part of the application process, the pupil’s most recent full school report must be submitted with the application (it must refer to his behaviour as well as his academic levels).
If the pupil’s application is accepted, but there is no place at the school at that specific time, the parents will be offered a place on the waiting list and will be notified as soon as a place becomes available.
There are a number of policies in place to ensure that the school runs efficiently. These can be found on the Policies & Documents page. Hard copies are also available on request from the school office.
How to apply: step by step
New pupils start in early September.
Over 16 applications (Year 12 and above)
Over 16 applications may be made at any stage. A request for a written reference, together with predicted GCSE or IGCSE grades, is made from the applicant’s present or previous school.
Criteria for admission
Darul Uloom London welcomes applications from pupils of all abilities. At present our facilities for pupils with disabilities are limited, but we will do all that is reasonable to ensure that the school’s culture, policies and procedures are accessible to pupils with disabilities, and we make reasonable adjustments to our admissions procedures in line with the Equality Act 2010. Information about a pupil’s health, disability or additional needs is used only to plan support and reasonable adjustments, never as a filter for admission.
The academic criteria for selection are: passing the entry tests; a good report from the pupil’s current school; and a positive interview. We are looking for well-rounded role models and proud citizens.
When the school is oversubscribed and we have to decide between applicants who meet our requirements, we may give preference to a pupil with better entry-test results, an earlier date of application, or an outstanding school report.
A place is confirmed once the application and registration fees have been paid and the first instalment of fees has been received, as set out in the Fee Policy. The fee schedule and the Fee Policy are sent to parents with the offer letter.
For all admission enquiries, please email education@darululoomlondon.com or telephone 020 8295 0637.
How to apply
To apply, download our Student Application Form using the button below. You can type into it on screen, or print it and complete it by hand.
The form is in five parts: Part A is completed by the parent or guardian, with the student questionnaire completed by the student himself; Part B is completed by the student’s current school and Part C by his current maktab or madrasah – please pass those pages to them, and they may return them to us directly; Part D sets out the application terms and conditions; and Part E is the application declaration, signed by the parents or guardians and the student.
Type into the boxes on screen and save the file, or print it and complete it in block capitals. Return the completed form to education@darululoomlondon.com, or hand it in at the school office, with a copy of the student’s birth certificate and/or passport and his latest school report, stamped by the school. Applications are not processed until everything has been received.
What happens next. Once we have the completed form, both reports and the documents, we will contact you to arrange an interview and open day. Offers are confirmed in writing with a start date, the book list and the fee schedule.
Before you apply, please read the terms and conditions of application and the application declaration below. They are the same terms and declaration as Parts D and E of the application form.
Terms and conditions of application
Read with the school’s policies. Acceptance of a place reserves it for the whole academic year, and the full annual fee, including VAT where applicable, becomes payable once the student starts; no refund, reduction or credit is given for withdrawal, absence, illness, holidays or exclusion, and a full term’s written notice of withdrawal is asked for. Attendance is a legal requirement: leave in term time is granted only in strict circumstances and must be requested by email at least 72 hours ahead, term-time holidays are recorded as unauthorised absence, and boarders must be back in school and signed in by 5.30pm after weekends at home (Attendance Policy; Boarders’ Booklet). Medicines are handed in to staff on arrival, and a student with a condition needing emergency medicine must have a current care plan and the medicine with him on the first day of term (Care of Boarders Who Are Unwell Policy). The school follows Keeping Children Safe in Education and may share information with the local authority and other agencies as the law requires (Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy). Personal data is handled in line with the Data Protection Policy and Privacy Notice. The school reviews its policies each year; the current versions are available from the school office.
Application declaration
I wish for my son to be admitted for education at Darul Uloom London. I have seen, and am satisfied with, the accommodation, school policies, facilities, food and other arrangements, and with the school’s functions. I declare that:
I agree with all of the above completely and will always respect Darul Uloom London’s protocols and procedures. If any of the above conditions are not met or any rules are broken, the management has every right to suspend and/or expel my child.
How we use your information
The personal information you give in this application is used to process the application and, if a place is offered, to admit and educate your son, to keep him safe and to meet the school’s legal duties. Darul-Uloom London (registered charity 1043305) is the data controller. Please read our Privacy Notice, which explains what we hold, why, who we share it with, how long we keep it and your rights. Questions go to the Data Protection Lead, Abubakr Ahmed, at education@darululoomlondon.com.

Statement of Boarding Principles and Practice
At Darul Uloom London, we want every boarder to lead a fulfilling and happy life in a comfortable, spiritual and secure environment, so that he may progress in his religious and secular learning. This statement sets out the principles on which our boarding is run and how they work in practice. It is available to parents, carers and staff, is explained to every new boarder and summarised in the Boarders’ Booklet, and the trustees check that it is followed in practice.
Our boarding ethos
Darul Uloom London is an Islamic boarding school for boys. Boarders live, learn and worship together in an Islamic environment in which the teachings of Islam play a central role in their moral and spiritual development, and in which the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect for and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs are actively promoted. Boarders come from different places and backgrounds; we treat every boy with equal respect and expect the same of him, in line with our Equality, Accessibility and Religious, Dietary, Language and Cultural Needs Policy.
Who boarding is for and how boarders join us
Darul Uloom London welcomes pupils of differing abilities and interests, and we are happy to accept any boy who we feel will thrive in our friendly and caring environment. Admission is decided under the Admissions Policy, which is the single statement of how admissions work: each applicant is interviewed with his parents, sits entrance papers in English and mathematics, and a reference is obtained from his current school before a place is offered. The Principal is responsible for admissions.
Every new boarder is given an induction: he is shown his room, locker and classroom, meets his Housemaster and is given the Boarders’ Booklet, which explains boarding life in plain language and is reviewed each year with the school council. Staff and older pupils help new boarders to settle in, and boarding staff give particular attention to them during their first weeks.
Faith and daily life
Salah is prayed in congregation at its appointed time every day, the timetable is built around it, and all pupils are expected to attend prayers regularly and on time; this is part of the published daily routine that families accept on admission. Arrangements for any pupil of another faith or with particular needs are made under the Equality Policy, and participation expectations are applied with the accommodations that policy describes.
Three meals a day are served in the dining hall, the menu is displayed in advance, and particular religious, dietary, cultural and medical needs, including allergies, are catered for. Boarders may keep their own snacks in their lockers and use the kitchen facilities in the dining hall; food is not kept or eaten in the dormitories.
Welfare, health and support
Every boarder has adults he can turn to. Welfare support is provided through day-to-day mentoring by the boarding staff and the teachers, and any pupil may take a problem or concern to any member of staff, who will make time and find a private place to listen. Two independent listeners, who are not employed by the school, are available to all pupils for support and the confidential reporting of issues or concerns; their names and telephone numbers are displayed in every boarding area and in the Boarders’ Booklet, and a pupil may contact them at any reasonable time without giving a reason or asking permission. Childline and other free helplines are displayed alongside them.
Safeguarding is central to everything we do, and every member of staff shares responsibility for it. The Designated Safeguarding Lead is the Head of Boarding, supported by trained deputy DSLs, one of whom is always contactable during boarding hours, including overnight; they are named, with all safeguarding contacts, in the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy. Any boarding concern with a welfare element is recorded and linked to safeguarding records, and low-level concerns are recorded so that patterns can be seen.
First aid and the administration of medicines are provided by trained first aiders among the boarding and administration staff, who hold the competence set out in the Care of Boarders Who Are Unwell Policy and the staff training matrix. The school has a medical room; parents are told the same day of any first aid given and immediately of any head injury, and boarders may register with the local GP practice. Boarders’ mental health and emotional wellbeing are supported under the Pupil Mental Health and Wellbeing Policy, which names the school’s Mental Health Lead, and all staff are trained to recognise the warning signs of common mental health problems.
Keeping in touch with home, weekends and leave
Boarders can contact their parents and families in private: school telephones are available during break times, a quiet space is arranged on request, and parents may ring the school office at any reasonable time and are given emergency contact arrangements when their son starts. Personal mobile phones and other internet-enabled devices are not permitted, so contact with home is through the school’s arrangements, and the school’s computers and internet are filtered and monitored. Year 7 boarders go home every weekend and boarders from Year 8 go home every other weekend, returning and signing in by 5.30pm on the day of return; the weekends on which boarders stay are set out in the school holiday planner. At weekends on site, boarders over 16 may go to the local town centre with permission, signing out and back in and returning by the agreed time. Leave during term time is granted only as set out in the Attendance Policy.
Activities and free time
Boarding staff provide a programme of activities for evenings and weekends, and boarders have free time each day. Activities include football, basketball, pool, table tennis, carrom and jiu-jitsu, and clubs such as ICT and reading; the library, the masjid, the study rooms and the grounds are available to boarders who want quiet time, and the school council gathers boarders’ ideas for trips and activities. A varied weekly programme is displayed on the boarding noticeboard, activities that could put boarders at risk are risk-assessed, and the programme is reviewed each term with the school council.
Our aims for every boarder
Our aim for each pupil by the time he graduates is that he:
Appreciates, respects and honours the environment.
Behaviour, rewards and sanctions
We promote good behaviour through a simple and consistent system of positives and negatives, set out in the Behaviour, Character and Discipline Policy and displayed on the positives and negatives poster around the school. Positives are earned for good work, hifz, kindness, khidmah (service), a tidy room and much more, and are spent on rewards; negatives are recorded in the behaviour log with the reason, are always explained to the pupil at the time, and lead to weekend detention with a reflection activity. The Head of Boarding reviews the positive and behaviour logs each term, and an anonymised summary goes to the trustees.
Serious misconduct is dealt with under the categories in that policy. Exclusion is decided only by a panel of at least two members of the senior leadership team, including the Head of Boarding or the Principal, and every return from exclusion begins with a reintegration meeting. A pupil may appeal a negative or detention to the Head Housemaster, and for permanent exclusion parents have a final right of appeal to the trustees. Bullying in any form is not tolerated: every report is logged and acted on under the Countering Bullying Policy, and no pupil is ever in trouble for reporting in good faith. Where an incident involves bullying, discriminatory or sexualised conduct, child-on-child abuse, online harm or a repeated welfare concern, it is assessed for safeguarding implications under the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy and is never treated as a matter of discipline alone.
Boarders’ voice and complaints
Boarders are actively encouraged to contribute their views on how boarding is run. The school council, elected by the pupils, meets regularly with staff, and boarders’ views are gathered at least annually through the boarding survey and every day through conversations with their Housemasters; these views feed a boarding development plan reviewed by the Head of Boarding and reported to trustees, and boarders are told what has changed as a result. No boarder is penalised for raising a concern in good faith.
Complaints or concerns may be raised with any teacher or Housemaster, the Head of Boarding, the Designated Safeguarding Lead or the Principal through the school’s open-door approach, and formally under the Complaints Procedure, which is coordinated by the Head of Administration and includes a simple route for boarders to complain, in speech or in writing, to any trusted member of staff. The procedure explains how a complaint may be taken to the Chair of Trustees, to an appeal panel and, where appropriate, to the Department for Education. Written records of complaints are kept and reviewed for patterns.
Accommodation, privacy and supervision at night
Each boarder has his own bed, cupboard and lockable locker for his valuables, and is encouraged to personalise his bed space; bedrooms are checked regularly, and the accommodation is kept clean and in good repair through a maintenance log reviewed by the Head of Boarding. Staff respect boarders’ privacy: they knock and announce themselves before entering an occupied bedroom, except in an emergency, and enter sleeping areas at night only where necessary, in line with safeguarding good practice. Staff sleeping accommodation is separate from pupils’ sleeping areas, and no adult unconnected with the boarding staff team lives in or has unsupervised access to boarding accommodation. A member of boarding staff is on duty and contactable throughout the night; the duty rota and how to reach the member of staff on duty are displayed in each boarding area. Toilets and washing facilities provide appropriate privacy. CCTV is used for site security only, under the School CCTV Policy, and is never a substitute for staff supervision.
Boarders are taught what to do if the fire alarm sounds and take part in regular fire drills, including during boarding time; areas of the site that could be unsafe are out of bounds; visitors are signed in and supervised, and boarders never admit visitors to the boarding area; and boarders never leave the site without permission and always sign out and in.
Leadership, monitoring and review of boarding
Boarding is led day to day by the Head of Boarding, who reports to the Principal and to the Board of Trustees. The trustees monitor the effectiveness of boarding and welfare through regular monitoring visits, termly reports and anonymised summaries drawn from the behaviour, bullying, complaints and safeguarding logs, an annual boarding self-evaluation against the National Minimum Standards for Boarding Schools, and the boarding development plan; safeguarding, including boarding welfare, is a standing item at every trustee meeting, and the nominated safeguarding trustee meets the Designated Safeguarding Lead at least termly.
All staff and volunteers who work with boarders are recruited and checked under the Safer Recruitment Policy, have a job description covering their boarding duties, receive an induction in boarding and take part in training and regular reviews of their practice; no adult who has not been checked is left unsupervised with boarders. Trustees and senior staff have been trained in the National Minimum Standards and the Independent School Standards, and boarding practice is checked against this statement so that it is seen to work in practice.

A caring and child-centred pastoral care provision lies at the heart of Darul Uloom London’s ethos and good practice. It is our priority that the pupils attending the school are safe and their welfare paramount. For this reason, a strong pastoral team has been assembled with the aim of supporting a child’s academic, behavioural and emotional development.
Our pastoral care system supports both the academic work of the pupil and his social and personal development. A happy pupil enjoying a settled, caring atmosphere will be well integrated, more secure and better motivated.
